The Community Living Center is comprised of Three (3) distinct neighborhoods: a 10-bed Hospice Unit, and a 66-bed combination Long Term Care/Short Stay Unit/Rehabilitation.

The program is designed to provide optimal comprehensive resident care within available resources and is consistent with the Health Care System and Nursing Service mission, philosophy, and goals. The length of stay for veterans in the unit may range from a few days to several years.

The length of stay is determined by the individual needs of the veteran, potential for rehabilitation, and availability of resources for discharge to the least restrictive environment. Discharge planning and patient/family education is initiated upon admission and continues throughout the veterans stay in the CLC.

The Community Living Center has an interdisciplinary team that includes staffing representing Nursing, Dietary, Social Work, Pharmacy, Occupational Therapy, Physical Therapy, Nurse Practitioners, and Physicians. The interdisciplinary team meets each week to discuss care planning and needs of patients.

Registered Nurses are competent in the management of patients with complex diseases such as Diabetes, CHF, COPD, Cancer, and Dementia. Staff receives education in other areas, including pain management and end of life care. The 4 (four) key quality characteristics of the Registered Nurse role are as follows: 1. Clinical knowledge and skills 2.

Rehab/restorative nursing abilities 3. Compliance with infection control guidelines 4. Critical thinking and care planning Preferred Qualifications: Minimum of one (1) year nursing home experience at the SNF level, in the role of Registered Nurse or Licensed Practical Nurse.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively with patients, families, and other members of the interdisciplinary team. Demonstrated skills in decision-making, sound clinical judgment and critical-thinking abilities. Demonstrated ability to use computer systems in support of patient care delivery.

The primary and single most important duty and responsibility of the Oncology/Hematology Registered Nurse (RN) is to administer intravenous (IV) medication infusions. IV medication infusion administration is an essential and central duty of the RN for promoting, achieving, and maintaining high-quality patient outcomes.

The Oncology/Hematology Registered RN is a clinical expert who uses advanced specialized knowledge and judgement for delivery of high quality and evidence-based care to oncology patients and their families. Uses a team approach to identify, analyze, and resolve patient care problems with measurable outcomes.

Completes physiological assessments and completes documentation in the electronic health record (EHR) in accordance to established policies and procedures. Triages patient problems and assists in the evaluation of symptoms and initiate interventions in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team.

Monitors, tracks/tends, and reports ongoing care needs and outcomes to the interdisciplinary team. They direct the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies, and providing quality improvement and outcome utilization.

They provide a safe working environment while administering, handling, and disposing of antineoplastic drugs and medical waste. They oversee the administration and management of various medical procedures and treatments in the oncology setting, including vascular access devices and infusion treatments.

Conducts in-service education based on insights gained from oncology professional development activities and acquiring specialized skills in oncology-specific areas, including chemotherapy administration, oncology electronic ordering systems, and calculating drug dosages.

The Oncology/Hematology RN manages monitoring requirements for specific drugs, handling immediate infusion reactions, and preventing and managing oncology-related symptoms and adverse events, such as chemo-related symptoms and immune-related adverse events.

The Domiciliary Mental Health (MH) Registered Nurse (RN) executes position responsibilities to improve patient and organizational outcomes.

The domiciliary RN executes their position duties by providing patient-centered and recovery-oriented care and maintaining self-awareness while caring for patients living with substance use disorder and/or MH conditions.

The domiciliary RN facilitates shift reports, warm hand-offs, and develops content as well as facilitates nurse-led psychoeducational groups. They use therapeutic communication techniques, practices de-escalation techniques, utilizes recovery-oriented language, and provides oversight of the patient safe medication management program.

The domiciliary RN demonstrates the ability to work with and lead MH interdisciplinary teams and work collaboratively with others as well as independently.

They promote critical thinking, participates in patient safety and environment of care rounds, directs team response to psychiatric and medical care needs and emergencies, reports safety concerns, and assists and/or directs safety concern resolution.

The domiciliary RN documents nursing assessments, risk screens, measurement-based care tools, nursing plan of care, patient safety rounds, and environment of care rounds according to facility policy. The domiciliary RN maintains professional boundaries to protect patient vulnerabilities and act in the best interest of the patient.

Provides peers with formal or informal constructive feedback for improvement. Supports colleagues and other nurses through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care. Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of health care professionals.

The responsibilities of the HBPC RN include, but are not limited to: Demonstrates leadership, experience, and creative approaches to the management of HBPC clients with complex needs who live in their own homes or other community settings. Performs activities as outlined in the Nurse Qualification Standards.

In this complex role, exhibits flexibility, sound judgment, independent problem solving and decision making, as well as collaboration with an interdisciplinary team of primary care providers in health promotion and disease prevention.

Must be a skilled clinician who demonstrates leadership in patient advocacy, provides, coordinates, facilitates, and improves patient care and customer service through health promotion and disease prevention as well as providing direct patient care utilizing protocols for selected disease management programs.

Uses sound judgment in assessing, planning, implementing, documenting and evaluating patient care and accurately documents and reports care -Identifies, analyzes and resolves patient care problems whose resolution results in the significant improvement of care to individual and/or groups of patients.

The incumbent achieves these objectives through: Appropriate application of current concepts to clinical practice Implementation of case management principles Effective application of interpersonal relationship skills A customer service focus Coordination of the interdisciplinary team effort toward quality patient care Integrity and assessing performance measures within his/her scope of practice.

This clinical position includes a level of physicality normally associated with direct patient care duties performed by nurses such as potentially long periods of continued walking, standing, sitting, moderate lifting, repeated bending, or kneeling.

Examples may include but are not limited to: Significant amounts of time standing assisting assigned patients Utilization of safe patient handling and mobility protocols Supervisory Controls: The incumbent is responsible to the assigned rating and approving supervisors and is accountable to the Associate Director of Patient Care Services (ADPCS).

General Description of Assigned Duties: The Emergency Department Registered Nurse Manager functions as a clinical expert and is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing or supervising direct patient care. Assesses, plans, implements, and evaluates delivery of care based on age specific components.

Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care. They demonstrate sound decision-making and judgment and possess excellent interpersonal skills.

They are self-directed and influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team and leading innovative process improvement initiatives. Executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex client care.

Functions or Scope of Assigned Duties: The Nurse Manager is the designated first-line supervisory authority and is responsible and accountable for the operation of their assigned units and provides coverage for other Nurse Managers as needed.

The Nurse Manager is responsible and accountable for the direction and supervision of specific orientation, training, development of staff, and evaluation of individual staff performance. Functions as a role model, educator, practitioner, and supervisor providing leadership to the team.

Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team to remove barriers and implement new evidence-based cutting-edge programs/processes. The Nurse Manager engages in professional organizations to enhance leadership and career growth.

Adheres to ethical principles in decision-making, fostering accountability at personal, organizational, and staff levels. Equips staff with tools for competent care and promotes an environment of accountability for high-quality, cost-effective outcomes.

Promotes alliances across the care continuum, building trust through active listening, engagement, and emotional intelligence. Contributes to the development of care delivery models and environmental design, ensuring evidence-based, accessible, affordable, and equitable patient care. Ensures compliance with accreditation and regulatory standards.

Aligns nursing and clinical objectives with organizational strategic outcomes, participating in strategy planning and execution. Promotes a workplace positively to achieve the organization's vision and mission.

The Nurse Manager maintains knowledge and ensures compliance with all regulatory and accreditation standards, directives, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOP). **Sinnvolle Arbeit. Echtes Miteinander. Raum, um etwas zu bewegen.**
**Willkommen bei der Stiftung WFJB**
Jeder Mensch verdient die Möglichkeit, sein Leben selbstbestimmt zu gestalten. Genau dafür setzen wir uns täglich mit Herz, Fachkompetenz und Engagement ein.
Die Stiftung WFJB ist ein Kompetenzzentrum für Menschen mit einer Hirnverletzung oder einer körperlichen Beeinträchtigung. Mit unseren Angeboten in den Bereichen Wohnen, Tagesstruktur, Arbeit, Freizeit sowie Betreuung und Pflege schaffen wir Lebensräume, in denen Menschen ihre Fähigkeiten entfalten, Beziehungen leben und am gesellschaftlichen Leben teilhaben können.
Für das Wohnhuus Meilihof in Ebertswil suchen wir nach Vereinbarung eine engagierte Persönlichkeit als
Pflegefachperson HF für den Nachtdienst
**Warum du gerne bei uns arbeiten wirst**
Bei uns bist du Teil eines Teams, das füreinander einsteht und gemeinsam etwas bewirkt und trotzdem arbeitest du in der Nacht alleine. Wir begegnen uns auf Augenhöhe, vertrauen einander und schaffen ein Arbeitsumfeld, in dem Menschen wachsen können - die betreuten Personen genauso wie die Mitarbeitenden.
**Darauf kannst du dich freuen:**
* Eine sinnstiftende Tätigkeit mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum und Eigenverantwortung.
* Zeit für eine individuelle und ganzheitliche Begleitung der betreuten Personen in der Nacht.
* Ein wertschätzendes Arbeitsklima mit einer offenen Du-Kultur.
* Ein engagiertes Team, das Wissen teilt, sich gegenseitig unterstützt und gemeinsam Erfolge feiert.
* Vielfältige Möglichkeiten zur fachlichen und persönlichen Weiterentwicklung.
* Moderne Arbeitsmittel und ein praxiserprobtes Qualitätsmanagement.
* Attraktive Anstellungsbedingungen sowie geregelte Arbeitszeiten
**Deine Aufgabe**
Du begleitest Menschen mit einer Hirnverletzung oder körperlichen Beeinträchtigung in der Nacht und stellst sicher, dass sie sich sicherfühlen. Dabei orientierst du dich an ihren individuellen Bedürfnissen, Ressourcen und Wünschen.
**Zu deinen Aufgaben gehören:**
* Ganzheitliche Begleitung der betreuten Personen als alleinige Nachtwache.
* Stellvertretende Übernahme von Tätigkeiten des alltäglichen Lebens.
* Erhaltung und Förderung von Selbstständigkeit, Selbstbestimmung und sozialer Teilhabe.
* Verantwortungsbewusste Umsetzung des Medikamentenmanagements.
* Administrative Aufgaben in Zusammenarbeit mit der tagesverantwortlichen Fachperson.
**Das bringst du mit**
Du arbeitest verantwortungsbewusst, selbstständig und verlierst auch in anspruchsvollen Situationen den Überblick nicht. Menschen begegnest du mit Respekt, Empathie und einer positiven Grundhaltung.
**Ausserdem bringst du mit:**
* Freude an der Arbeit mit Menschen mit einer Beeinträchtigung.
* Humor, Geduld und die Fähigkeit, Beziehungen vertrauensvoll zu gestalten.
* Organisationstalent und gute Kommunikationsfähigkeiten.
* Interesse an interdisziplinärer Zusammenarbeit.
**Gemeinsam Lebensqualität gestalten**
Jede Nacht bietet neue Begegnungen, neue Herausforderungen und viele kleine Momente, die Grosses bewirken. Wenn du deine Fachkompetenz mit Herz einbringen möchtest und eine Aufgabe suchst, die Sinn stiftet, freuen wir uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.
**Bewirb dich jetzt**
Sende deine vollständigen Bewerbungsunterlagen inklusive Foto an:
Wohnhuus Meilihof, Nathalie Mannino, Dorfstrasse 3c, 8925 Ebertswil.
E-Mail: nathalie.mannino@meilihof.ch

**Infirmier(-ère) de jour en Médecine - CDM 6 mois à 60% (ref : 2013)**
**Votre mission :**
Dans un établissement de pointe vous occupez un poste varié au sein d'une équipe pluridisciplinaire comprenant des infirmiers(-ères), des aides-soignants(-es), des médecins.
Vous devrez assurer l-accueil des patients atteints de pathologies polyvalentes, dans le cadre d-une prise en charge globale en phase aigüe.
A ce titre vous êtes en charge de ;
* Installer le patient et lui présenter les informations d'organisation administrative et de soin
* Recueillir et transmettre les données médicales et administratives et compléter le dossier de soins informatisé
* Assurer et organiser la planification des soins en fonction des priorités et du degré d'urgence
* Effectuer les soins sur prescription médicale et en conformité avec les procédures de l-unité et institutionnelles
* Assurer la tenue du Dossier Patient Informatisé
* Evaluer continuellement l'état clinique du patient et son évolution en situation aigue
* Identifier les situations de fragilité, de perte d'autonomie et de complexité nécessitant une approche interdisciplinaire ;
* Participer à la prise en charge de patients âgés et polymorbides, ainsi qu'à l'accompagnement de patients et de leurs proches confrontés à des situations palliatives ;
* Collaborer avec les différents intervenants afin d'assurer la continuité et la coordination des soins ;
* Assurer la coordination inter services pour la gestion des mouvements de patients
* Coordonner les entrées et sorties : les mutations internes, les transferts externes des patients en collaboration avec le cadre de santé.
**Nous recherchons un profil répondant aux critères suivants :**
* Diplôme d'infirmier(-ère)
* En possession de la reconnaissance croix rouge si diplôme étranger
* Disposant d'une expérience en médecine interne, en gériatrie, en soins palliatifs ou dans un domaine de soins complexes, un atout ;
* Présentant un intérêt marqué pour la prise en charge des patients âgés, polymorbides et/ou en situation palliative ;
* Sensible à l'approche globale et interdisciplinaire du patient ;
* Sens du contact et du service dans le cadre d'un établissement privé
* Autonome, bienveillance, polyvalence, capacité d'adaptation, d'organisation et sens des priorités sont des qualités essentielles
* Attitude positive au sein d'une équipe et êtes capable de générer un climat de confiance
* Capable de contribuer à instaurer un climat de confiance avec les patients, leurs proches et les différents professionnels.
**Un environnement en évolution**
Rejoindre notre équipe, c'est intégrer un service de médecine interne dynamique, au cœur d'un environnement en développement, offrant la possibilité de contribuer à l'évolution de nouvelles filières de soins.
